subject: Archaeology
title: The Copper Scroll: A Real Treasure Map
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Copper Scroll: A Real Treasure Map.

hook.text: Among the Dead Sea Scrolls was a copper sheet listing 64 locations where gold and silver are supposedly hidden.

buildup.text: Found in 1952 at Qumran, the Copper Scroll is unique among the Dead Sea Scrolls — it is not religious but a practical.

discovery.text: The locations use landmarks that no longer exist: 'in the gutter under the east wall,' 'in the cistern under.

twist.text: Many expeditions have searched the listed locations. No treasure has ever been found.

climax.text: Some scholars believe the treasure was Jerusalem's Temple wealth hidden before the Roman invasion of 70 CE.

punchline.text: A 2,000-year-old treasure map with 64 locations. Not one ounce has been found.

quiz.question: What might the Copper Scroll's treasure represent?
options: Jerusalem's Temple wealth hidden before the Roman invasion of 70 CE
Offerings collected by the Essene community at Qumran
